simple: the short list of numbers that tells you everything about a machine right now that matters for what it does next.
analogy: where the rider is, how fast she goes, how far the bike leans, and how fast the lean grows.
precise: a vector x(t) ∈ ℝ^n such that x(t_0) and the input u on [t_0, t] determine x(t) and the output for all t ≥ t_0; MA301 F0-67 introduced it as the state of a dynamic system.
source: B1, U1 of F9-59 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: four tables of numbers that say how the state changes and what the sensors see.
analogy: the rider's inner rule book: "if I lean this much and push the pedal this hard, next moment I will lean that much".
precise: the linear time-invariant model x′ = Ax + Bu, y = Cx + Du with A ∈ ℝ^n×n (dynamics), B ∈ ℝ^n×m (input), C ∈ ℝ^p×n (output), D ∈ ℝ^p×m (direct feed-through).
source: B1 of F9-59 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a state where the machine would stay forever if nothing disturbed it.
analogy: the bicycle perfectly upright; a breath of wind tips it over, so it is an unstable equilibrium.
precise: a pair (x_e, u_e) with f(x_e, u_e) = 0 for x′ = f(x, u).
source: B1 of F9-59 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: replacing a curved rule by a straight-line rule that is good near one point.
analogy: the rider's rule "a little more lean needs a little more correction", which is only true for small leans.
precise: for small deviations δx = x − x_e, δu = u − u_e, δx′ ≈ A δx + B δu with A = ∂f/∂x and B = ∂f/∂u evaluated at (x_e, u_e) (Jacobian matrices).
source: B1, D1 of F9-59 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: special directions in which the system just grows or shrinks (or spins) at its own rate, without turning into another direction.
analogy: the "falling over" motion of the bike, which grows on its own, at its own speed.
precise: λ ∈ ℂ and v ≠ 0 with Av = λv; the eigenvalues are the roots of det(λI − A) = 0. For x′ = Ax they are the poles of the system (MA301 F0-69).
source: B1, D1 of F9-59 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the rule that carries the state forward by a chosen time when nobody pushes.
analogy: "if I do nothing for one second, this is where I will be".
precise: e^At = I + At + (At)²/2! + (At)³/3! + …; the solution of x′ = Ax is x(t) = e^Atx(0).
source: B1, D1 of F9-59 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the same rule book, written for a computer that looks and acts only every T seconds.
analogy: a rider who blinks: she sees only snapshots and holds her steering still between them.
precise: x[k+1] = A_dx[k] + B_du[k] with A_d = e^AT and B_d = (∫_0^T e^Aτdτ) B, exact when u is held constant over each period (zero-order hold, MA302 F0-79).
source: B1, D1 of F9-59 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a cart that must keep a stick standing upright by moving under it.
analogy: balancing a bicycle by steering under its lean.
precise: a cart of mass M on a horizontal track, driven by a horizontal force F, carrying a pole hinged at the cart; in this course a massless rod of length l with a point mass m at its end; four states (x, v, θ, ω), one input F.
source: D1 of F9-59 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the inputs can push the machine from any state to any other state in a finite time.
analogy: your muscles can reach every part of your balance and position.
precise: the pair (A, B) is controllable if for every x_0, x_f and some finite time there is an input taking x(0) = x_0 to x(t_f) = x_f; for linear time-invariant systems this holds exactly when the controllability matrix has rank n.
source: B1 of F9-60 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a table that lists every direction the input can push the state: directly, after one step of the dynamics, after two, and so on.
analogy: where a push on the handlebar takes the bike now, a moment later, and a moment after that.
precise: W_c = [B, AB, A²B, …, A^n−1B] ∈ ℝ^n×nm.
source: B1, D1 of F9-60 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: by watching the sensors for a while (and knowing the inputs) you can work out the whole state.
analogy: from what your senses feel you can tell your lean, its rate, your speed and where you are.
precise: the pair (A, C) is observable if the output y on a finite interval, with u known, determines x(0) uniquely; for LTI systems, exactly when the observability matrix has rank n. Not the same as observability in distributed systems (DS402), which means being able to understand a running service from its logs, metrics and traces.
source: B1 of F9-60 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a table of what the sensors see of the state now, and of how it changes over the next steps.
analogy: what your senses report now, and a moment later.
precise: W_o = [C; CA; CA²; …; CA^n−1] ∈ ℝ^np×n.
source: B1, D1 of F9-60 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one of the basic motions a system can make on its own, each with its own rate.
analogy: "falling over", "rolling along", "two bikes leaning apart".
precise: a solution e^λtv of x′ = Ax with Av = λv; a mode is uncontrollable if no input can excite or cancel it, unobservable if it leaves no trace in y.
source: B1, D1 of F9-60 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a test that checks each mode separately: can the input touch this one?
analogy: testing each wobble of the bike: can the handlebar affect this wobble at all?
precise: (A, B) is controllable if and only if rank [λI − A, B] = n for every eigenvalue λ of A; dually, (A, C) is observable if and only if rank [λI − A; C] = n for every λ.
source: B1 of F9-60 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the parts you cannot reach (or cannot see) at least settle down by themselves.
analogy: you cannot reach a wobble, but it dies out on its own, so you do not need to.
precise: (A, B) is stabilisable if every uncontrollable mode has Re λ < 0 (|z| < 1 in discrete time); (A, C) is detectable if every unobservable mode does. These are the weakest conditions under which a state-feedback controller, respectively an observer, can be made stable.
source: B1 of F9-60 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the gentlest input that still gets the state where you want it; how big it is tells you how hard that move is.
analogy: the smallest effort with which you could bring two bikes into a chosen lean.
precise: for x[N] = R u with R = [A_d^N−1B_d, …, B_d], the input of least Σu² reaching x_f is u = Rᵀ(RRᵀ)^−1x_f; RRᵀ is the N-step reachability Gramian, and its small eigenvalues mark directions that are expensive to reach.
source: B1, D1 of F9-60 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the controller looks at the whole state and sets the input as a weighted sum of all of it.
analogy: Nadia's rule: so much steering for the lean, so much for the lean rate, so much for her drift and speed.
precise: u = −Kx (or u = −K(x − r) with a reference r), K ∈ ℝ^m×n; the closed loop is x′ = (A − BK)x.
source: B1, D1 of F9-61 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: choosing the gains so that the controlled machine's natural motions have exactly the speeds you asked for.
analogy: deciding how fast a lean should die away, then finding the reaction strengths that make it so.
precise: given (A, B) and a set Λ of n numbers closed under complex conjugation, find K with eig(A − BK) = Λ; possible for every Λ exactly when (A, B) is controllable.
source: B1 of F9-61 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the polynomial whose roots are the closed-loop poles; its coefficients are what the gains change.
analogy: the recipe that sets every speed of the ride at once.
precise: det(sI − (A − BK)) = s^n + a_1s^n−1 + … + a_n; pole placement matches it to the desired Π(s − λ_i).
source: D1 of F9-61 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a formula that gives the gain row directly from the model and the desired poles, for one input.
analogy: a ready-made rule-maker: give it the bike and the ride you want, it gives the reaction strengths.
precise: K = [0 … 0 1] W_c^−1 φ(A), where W_c is the controllability matrix and φ is the desired characteristic polynomial.
source: B1 of F9-61 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a way to write a single-input model so that the characteristic polynomial's coefficients appear directly in A.
analogy: rearranging the bike's controls so each knob turns exactly one coefficient.
precise: a change of coordinates z = Tx giving A_c with ones on the superdiagonal and −a_n, …, −a_1 in the last row, and B_c = [0, …, 0, 1]ᵀ; it exists exactly when (A, B) is controllable.
source: B1 of F9-61 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: to go one way, the system must first move the other way.
analogy: to turn a bicycle left, you first steer slightly right so the bike leans left.
precise: a step response that starts in the opposite direction to its final value, caused by a transfer-function zero in the right half-plane (for the cart-pole, between F and x).
source: B1, R3 of F9-61 (R: real lab runs of the chapter; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a score that adds up, at every sample, how far the state is from where you want it and how hard the controller pushes, each squared and weighted.
analogy: Tomás's "staying on the line matters a lot, jerking the bars matters little".
precise: J = Σ_k≥0 (x[k]ᵀQx[k] + u[k]ᵀRu[k]) with Q symmetric positive semidefinite and R symmetric positive definite.
source: B1 of F9-62 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the state-feedback gain that makes the quadratic cost as small as possible for a linear model.
analogy: the riding style Nadia settles into once she knows what matters.
precise: for x[k+1] = Ax[k] + Bu[k], the minimiser of J over all input sequences is u[k] = −Kx[k] with K = (R + BᵀPB)^−1BᵀPA, where P solves the discrete algebraic Riccati equation.
source: B1, D1 of F9-62 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the matrix equation whose solution gives the best gain.
analogy: the bookkeeping that tells Nadia what every lean will cost her from now on.
precise: P = Q + AᵀPA − AᵀPB(R + BᵀPB)^−1BᵀPA; under stabilisability of (A, B) and detectability of (A, Q^1/2) it has exactly one solution P ⪰ 0 that makes A − BK stable.
source: B1 of F9-62 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a matrix that tells you, for any starting state, the total cost the best controller will still pay.
analogy: how much trouble a given lean is going to be, before you have done anything about it.
precise: J*(x_0) = x_0ᵀPx_0, with P the stabilising DARE solution.
source: D1, R1 of F9-62 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; R: real lab runs of the chapter) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a first guess for the weights: one over the square of the largest value you can accept.
analogy: "on this bridge I can drift 20 cm at most" becomes the weight on drift.
precise: Q_ii = 1/(x_i,max)², R_jj = 1/(u_j,max)², off-diagonal entries zero; a starting point to be tuned, not an optimum.
source: B1 of F9-62 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an "energy" that is positive everywhere except at rest and always goes down along the motion, which proves the motion settles.
analogy: a measure of trouble that only ever shrinks while Nadia rides.
precise: V(x) = xᵀPx with P ≻ 0 and V(x[k+1]) − V(x[k]) = −x[k]ᵀ(Q + KᵀRK)x[k] < 0 for x ≠ 0 proves asymptotic stability of the closed loop.
source: B1, D1 of F9-62 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how late the controller's commands may arrive before the loop becomes unstable.
analogy: how slow Nadia's reactions can get before she starts to wobble.
precise: the largest delay d (here in samples between computing u[k] and applying it) for which the closed loop with that delay is still stable; for sampled loops, the largest d with spectral radius < 1.
source: B1, R3 of F9-62 (R: real lab runs of the chapter; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a program that runs a copy of the robot's model alongside the robot, and nudges the copy towards the sensor readings, so that the copy's state can stand in for states nobody measures.
analogy: Nadia's guess of her speed and lean rate, kept up to date by what she feels.
precise: x̂[k+1] = A_dx̂[k] + B_du[k] + L(y[k] − Cx̂[k]); the estimation error e = x − x̂ obeys e[k+1] = (A_d − LC)e[k].
source: B1, D1 of F9-63 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how strongly each sensor surprise corrects each estimated state.
analogy: how much Nadia changes her guess when the bike leans more than she expected.
precise: the matrix L ∈ ℝ^n×p; its choice places the eigenvalues of A_d − LC, which is possible for any set exactly when (A_d, C) is observable.
source: B1 of F9-63 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the difference between what the sensors read and what the model expected them to read.
analogy: "it is leaning more than I thought".
precise: ν[k] = y[k] − Cx̂[k]; for a well-tuned observer it looks like the sensor noise, with no pattern left in it.
source: B1, D1 of F9-63 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: you can design the controller as if you had the true state, and the observer as if there were no controller; together they behave as each promised.
analogy: Nadia's riding rule and her guessing skill can be learned separately.
precise: for linear models, the closed loop of u = −Kx̂ with the observer above has the eigenvalues of A_d − B_dK together with those of A_d − LC.
source: B1, R3 of F9-63 (R: real lab runs of the chapter; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: control that uses only what the sensors measure, not the full state.
analogy: riding with your real senses, not with a magic display of every number.
precise: u is a function of y and past inputs only; here u = −Kx̂ with x̂ from an observer driven by y and u.
source: B1 of F9-63 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the observer gain that best balances how much the robot is pushed around against how noisy the sensors are.
analogy: trusting your feel more on a smooth road and your expectations more on a bumpy one.
precise: for process noise covariance W and sensor noise covariance V, L = Kᵀ of the LQR problem for (A_dᵀ, Cᵀ) with weights W and V (the dual Riccati equation); this form of the observer is a steady-state Kalman predictor. The full, time-varying Kalman filter is treated in RB302.
source: B1, B2 of F9-63 (B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: at every sample, use a model to plan the best sequence of inputs for the next stretch of time, respecting the limits; apply only the first input; repeat.
analogy: Nadia asking "if I keep going like this, can I still stop?" every moment.
precise: a feedback law u[k] = u_0*(x[k]) where u_0* is the first element of the minimiser of a finite-horizon optimal-control problem with constraints, solved online from the current state.
source: D1 of F9-64 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how far ahead the controller plans.
analogy: how far down the path Nadia looks.
precise: the number N of future samples (N·T seconds) over which the model predicts and the cost is summed.
source: D1 of F9-64 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the planning window slides forward one sample every time a new measurement arrives, so the plan is always for "the next N samples from now".
analogy: the stretch of path Nadia looks at moves with her.
precise: at sample k the problem covers k … k+N; only u[k] is applied; at k+1 a new problem over k+1 … k+N+1 is solved from the measured x[k+1].
source: D1 of F9-64 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a limit the plan must respect. A hard limit can never be crossed in the plan; a soft limit can be crossed at a high price.
analogy: the brakes' strength is hard (it is what it is); "don't touch the hedge" is soft (better not, but not impossible).
precise: hard: u[k] ∈ [−u_max, u_max] imposed exactly; soft: a penalty ρ·max(0, x − x_max)² added to the cost, which keeps the problem solvable even when the limit cannot be met.
source: D1 of F9-64 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an optimisation problem with a quadratic score and straight-line limits; the kind of problem a linear MPC must solve at every sample.
analogy: finding the lowest point of a smooth bowl, inside a fenced field.
precise: minimise UᵀHU + 2xᵀFᵀU subject to linear inequalities on U, with H symmetric positive definite.
source: D1 of F9-64 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a price on where the plan ends, standing in for everything after the horizon.
analogy: "and after those two seconds, how much trouble am I still in?"
precise: a term x[N]ᵀPx[N] in the cost; with P the solution of the LQR's Riccati equation, it is the exact unconstrained cost-to-go from x[N].
source: D1, B1 of F9-64 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; B: book sources, title only — not opened during this build) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: starting the solver from the previous plan, shifted by one sample, instead of from zero.
analogy: Nadia keeps most of her plan from a moment ago and only adjusts it.
precise: initialising the iterative QP solver at (u_1*, …, u_N−1*, u_N−1*) from the previous sample; it cuts the iterations needed when the state changes little between samples.
source: D1, R3 of F9-64 (D1: derivation shown in the chapter, recomputed by its lab runs; R: real lab runs of the chapter) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
